stance_basis: letter endorses Executive Order 11644 and proposed regulations but urges rejection of the proposed 'off-road vehicles' definition
summary: The Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Association (MVMA) filed comments endorsing the intent of Executive Order 11644 and the proposed regulations implementing it, but objected specifically to the proposed definition of 'off-road vehicles' as overly broad and potentially harmful to conventional highway vehicle use. MVMA urged that regulations be directed at the off-road use of vehicles rather than based on the problematic definition.
complaint_summary: MVMA endorses Executive Order 11644 and the proposed regulations but objects to the proposed definition of 'off-road vehicles' as broader than the Order suggests, all-encompassing, and potentially capable of inadvertently barring conventional highway vehicles from roads and highways, urging instead that regulations be directed to the off-road use of vehicles.

statement.text:
Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Association of the United States, Inc. (MVMA) is filing comments with the Bureau of Land Management and the Commissioner of Reclamation concerning the notices of proposed rule making that were published in the Federal Register of Wednesday, February 14, 1973. Copies of those comments are attached hereto.
On the same date, the Office of the Secretary published a notice (38 FR, NO. 30, Page 4422) reopening the review period for Draft Environmental Statement No. INT DES 72-62. MVMA hereby responds to the invitation for comment set forth in that notice.
MVMA is a trade association whose members manufacture more than 90% of the motor vehicles manufactured in the United States, which are designed primarily for use on streets, roads and highways. Our members' products include multipurpose passenger vehicles, trucks, buses, motor homes and the vehicle chassis used in the assembly of many types of recreational vehicles. A list of member companies is attached.
As we have stated in our comments to the Commissioner of Reclamation and to the Bureau of Land Management, this association endorses the intent expressed in Executive Order No. 11644 and in the proposed regulations which are intended to implement that Order.
We are concerned, however, that in the regulatory process a new definition, that of "off-road vehicles" may be published in the proposed regulations. A similar definition was proposed in the memorandum of May 5, 1972, from the Secretary of the Interior to Assistant Secretaries, on the implementation of Executive Order 11644. This definition would include among off-road vehicles any motorized vehicle (including the standard automobile) which may be used, or which is capable of being used, off established roadways.
113

Very truly yours,
This definition is broader than that suggested in Executive Order No. 11644, and is so all-encompassing as to be, in the opinion of this association, meaningless. Other definitions and classifications will still be required to regulate the use of various vehicles under different circumstances. The proposed definition, if adopted, may subsequently by inadvertance or accident, appear in regulations which would have the effect of barring the use of conventional highway vehicles even on roads and highways. It is for this reason that MVMA urges that the definition not be adopted, and that regulations be promulgated that are directed to the off-road use of vehicles, rather than to be based upon an unnecessary and confusing definition of "off-road vehicles".
Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Association appreciates the opportunity to submit comments in this rule making procedure.
